# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 26 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 36 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_026_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 26

**1** Jesus said: "You see the splinter in your brother's eye, but you do not see the beam in your own eye.

**2** When you remove the beam from your own eye, then you will see clearly to remove the splinter from your brother's eye."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**"Splinter" / "beam"** — LOGOS/EMET preferred over PNEUMA's "speck/plank." *Khob* = splinter (a wood chip); *šoit* = beam (a structural timber). "Splinter" is more accurate than "speck" (which implies dust rather than wood). "Beam" is the traditional English rendering, established in the Synoptic tradition.

**"See clearly"** — LOGOS preferred. The Coptic *ouōnh* carries the revelation/disclosure sense; your own vision is restored as a disclosure event.

**P.Oxy 1 parallel** — this is one of the three sayings attested in P.Oxy 1 (lines 1-4), confirming early attestation.

**Synoptic Parallels:**
- Matt 7:3-5: Nearly verbatim — "Why do you see the speck that is in your brother's eye, but do not notice the log that is in your own eye?" — Thomas and Matthew are almost identical
- Luke 6:41-42: Same saying
- This is among the most certain Q-tradition sayings also preserved in Thomas
